🐪 Good Wednesday afternoon. Today's newsletter, edited by Alex Fitzpatrick, is 711 words, a 2½-min. read. Thanks to Sheryl Miller for copy editing.

⚡️ Situational awareness: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent will host finance ministers and economic leaders from around the world, plus heavy-hitting U.S. CEOs, for the G20 Finance Ministerial in Asheville, N.C., from Aug. 29 to Sept. 1.

  • Bessent will use the summit in the Blue Ridge Mountains to emphasize the resilience of the American spirit — and push his global counterparts to focus on growth and prosperity. Sneak peek.
 
 
1 big thing: Washington's stealth oil operation
 
Illustration: Sarah Grillo/Axios. Stock: Getty Images

The U.S. military has quietly established a shipping corridor in and out of the Strait of Hormuz, two U.S. officials tell Axios' Barak Ravid.

🚢 Under the operation, which has been underway for the past several weeks, 15–20 tankers have entered and exited the strait through a southern channel along the coast of Oman.

  • About 10 million barrels of oil a day are being transported out of the strait and injected into the global energy market, the officials said. That's roughly half the pre-war volume.

⚓️ The U.S. military is helping empty tankers enter the Gulf from the Arabian Sea through the strait, pick up oil from the UAE, Bahrain and Kuwait, and then exit.

  • One of the U.S. officials, who has direct knowledge of the matter, tells Axios: "We have been controlling the southern lane of the Strait of Hormuz for two months now. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps can be a nuisance, but they don't control the strait. We do."

🪖 The task force overseeing the Hormuz effort is being run out of the Army's 82nd Airborne Division headquarters in Fort Bragg, N.C.

  • It creates a daily list of ships exiting the Gulf through the Strait of Hormuz and into the Arabian Sea, as well as a list of rented empty tankers that travel from the Arabian Sea, through the strait and into the ports of Gulf countries to pick up more oil.
  • Each night, the ships are scheduled to move in one big outbound line during a certain time slot and one big inbound line during a separate time slot.

The ships are given several checkpoints to pass through and report back.

  • The U.S. Air Force has fighter jets looking for Iranian cruise missiles and drones to shoot down.

2. 🤖 AI model hype goes wild
 
Illustration: Brendan Lynch/Axios. Stock: Getty Images

The online chatter about new AI models is starting to resemble the hype over the next Taylor Swift album or where LeBron James might end his career, Axios' Herb Scribner and Andrew Kay write.

🦁 The frenzy might start with a post from "leo," a reliable AI leaker with more than 34,000 followers.

  • Leo's posts can get picked up by Kim "Chubby" Isenberg, the Superintelligence editor-in-chief with more than 130,000 followers who's quick to aggregate AI chatter.

🤔 An AI writer, investor or CEO might throw in some speculation based on Chubby's post.

  • The timeline then becomes a free-flowing river of rumors, information and theories.

Reality check: As Swifties know all too well, the rumor mill is noisy and often wrong.

Which industries are investors turning to in the AI era?
 
 

As AI drives demand for infrastructure, stocks linked to capital-intensive businesses are winning favor with investors.

Also referred to as HALO stocks (Heavy Assets, Low Obsolescence), these companies are outperforming their capital-light peers.

Read more on HALO stocks.

 
 
3. ⚡️ Catch me up
 
President Trump signs a stone at the site of a new helipad on the White House South Lawn today. Photo: Jim Watson/AFP via Getty Images
  1. 🚁 President Trump gave journalists an impromptu look at his new helipad on the South Lawn of the White House this morning. He told reporters: "We have to bring the White House up to — like I'm fixing the country, we're fixing the White House too." Watch.
  2. 💊 Trump is nominating White House aide Heidi Overton to lead the FDA. He posted on Truth Social today: "We need her leadership at the FDA now to ensure that the U.S. remains the WORLD LEADER for Scientific Discovery and CURES." Go deeper.
  3. 📦 Amazon plans to bring rapid Prime Air drone deliveries to nearly 500 U.S. towns and cities by the end of this year. Go deeper.
  4. 🛰️ NASA is calling off a mission to save a space observatory falling out of orbit, dooming it to a fiery death in Earth's atmosphere. Go deeper.
 
 
4. 🍌 1 for the road: Coffee goes bananas
 
Illustration: Sarah Grillo/Axios

Banana is the flavor of the summer, Axios' Carly Mallenbaum reports.

  • It's the fastest-growing added beverage flavor over the past year at restaurants tracked by Circana, a market research firm.

📈 Google searches for "banana coffee" and "banana matcha" hit all-time highs this year.

  • TikTok has plenty of videos for the banana-curious — including Eva Longoria's tutorial for making banana iced coffee at home.

Go deeper.

How do geopolitical alliances affect global economic growth?
 
 

Measures of geopolitical risk and fragmentation have risen sharply since 2010, with some now sitting close to record highs.

Over the past decade, this rising fragmentation has cut an estimated 1% from global GDP, according to Goldman Sachs Research.
